newsitem.title: USA: Mace Security in talks over control.
newsitem.headline: Mace Security in talks over control.

text.p: Mace Security International Inc said on Wednesday that some of the company's top executives were negotiating the sale of their stakes in Mace to a leading competitor. Combined, the stakes represent a controlling interest in Mace.
The privately held competitor was not named.
Chairman Jon Goodrich is negotiating the sale of his 29.2 percent stake, and Robert Gould, a director, is negotiating the sale of his 27 percent stake, Mace said.

It said Executive Vice President Richard Galt was negotiating with the competitor over his option to acquire Goodrich's stake in Mace. The option, which expires September 2, requires the initial purchase of 640,000 shares, with the remaining shares available for purchase over four years, it said.
Also, the option holder has the right to vote the shares available under the option during a three-year period, it said.
There have been no discussions with the potential purchaser regarding the acquisition of the shares of any other Mace shareholders, Mace said.
